title: Introduce RAG schema-driven playbook and tool contract examples
author: Marisol Ortega
description: Context: teams building retrieval-augmented agents often end up with ad-hoc tool interfaces and brittle integration tests. This PR introduces a small, opinionated pattern: define playbooks and tool contracts as JSON Schemas, generate typed bindings from those schemas, and provide a minimal contract test runner so tool implementations can be validated against the declared contract. Motivation: improve developer ergonomics for agent/tool integration, make examples testable, and provide a path from authoring to CI validation without heavy infra. What changed: - Add a new example workspace under redwood-examples/rag-schema-playbook with a canonical playbook/schema pair, two sample tool-contracts (search and email sender), and a set of fixtures and smoke scenarios. - Include a simple TypeScript type generator script (examples/scripts/generate-types.sh) that emits typed bindings and a tiny runtime helper (ts-bindings/index.ts) for wiring tool calls into the playbook runtime. - Add contract-based Jest tests (tests/contract.test.ts) that verify a stub tool implementation satisfies the contract. - Add docs to redwood-docs/content/rag/schemas.md with authoring guidance and recommended patterns. - Add a lightweight CI workflow (.github/workflows/rag-examples-ci.yml) that runs contract tests and the typegen step. - Add a devcontainer for onboarding and a small sample index to run local RAG scenarios. Checklist: - [x] Schema definitions for playbook and tools - [x] Type generation script + example output - [x] Contract tests + CI workflow - [x] Authoring guide in docs - [x] Devcontainer and sample fixtures How to use: 1) Clone and open devcontainer, 2) run examples/scripts/generate-types.sh to emit bindings, 3) run npm test in rag-schema-playbook to run contract tests, 4) try the example playbook against the mini-index in examples/sample-index/mini-index.json. Backwards compatibility: this is additive and only adds example artifacts and docs. No change to runtime or public APIs. Related: ENG-2148 for long-term roadmap on typed tool APIs. Notes for reviewers: I aimed for the smallest possible runtime surface so teams can adopt the pattern independently. If we like this shape, we can later move the typegen into a shared devtool and expand language targets.
